speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition better, can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities in detail, and did it start before or after your fever and respiratory symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Can you describe the appearance of the facial rash, and has it since spread to involve the palms of her hands or soles of her feet?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The "slapped cheek" facial rash with sparing of the perioral area, followed by a lacy, pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, is highly characteristic of Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease), which is caused by Parvovirus B19. The preceding mild prodrome of fever, headache, and rhinorrhea also fits this clinical picture perfectly.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
